summary: Native macOS terminal built on Ghostty for running many AI coding agents at once, with vertical tabs, attention alerts and a built-in browser.

heroCommands.command: brew tap manaflow-ai/cmux && brew install --cask cmux
Download the DMG from the latest release

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: cmux is a macOS terminal app for people running several Claude Code or Codex sessions in parallel. A sidebar of vertical tabs shows each workspace's git branch, linked PR, folder, listening ports and latest notification, and panes light up with a blue ring when an agent needs you. It also has a scriptable in-app browser, SSH workspaces and one-command Claude Code teammate mode.
sixtySeconds.problem: With many agents running in split panes, it's hard to know which one is waiting for you and why. cmux surfaces that in the sidebar and a notification panel.
whoFor: Developers running many coding agents in parallel
Claude Code and Codex users on macOS
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a fast native Swift/AppKit app (not Electron) that reads your Ghostty config and is scriptable through a CLI and socket API.

overview: Install the DMG and drag cmux to Applications (it auto-updates), or use the Homebrew cask. The cask also installs shell completions for zsh, bash and fish.

Workspaces, splits and the browser are all controllable from the cmux CLI and socket API. cmux ssh creates a workspace for a remote machine, and cmux claude-teams runs Claude Code teammates as native splits.
The app is GPL-3.0-or-later; the cmux server software uses the Business Source License, as described in LICENSE.
limitations: Server components use a different license
